translations.answer: The original poster confirmed two issues: the negative direction joint axes in URDF need to be multiplied by -1 at the corresponding DOF positions; the NECK_Y import position disrupts the order of the upper arm joints, requiring adjustment of the order of the worldbody in MuJoCo XML and the ROTATION_AXIS to be in the same order. Only changing the sign of one axis is insufficient to fix the index misalignment. This conclusion was verified on a 30-joint custom humanoid robot and needs re-validation when migrating to other models.
translations.applicability: Applies to custom humanoid re-directions where joint axis signs and DOF ordering are explained via separate ROTATION_AXIS tables.
translations.credibility.rationale: Environmental, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: The questioner first modified the axis sign, but no change occurred; then both the sign matrix of dof_pos and joint order were adjusted.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Compare joint axis signs in URDF with runtime ROTATION_AXIS; print the joint order after import to confirm if NECK_Y is inserted before the upper arm DOF and causes index misalignment.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Create a sign matrix for negative-axis joints in URDF, multiply corresponding dof_pos by -1; adjust the order of NECK_Y in MuJoCo XML worldbody and modify the ROTATION_AXIS in torch_humanoid_batch.py accordingly.
translations.details.environments.0: LeCAR-Lab/human2humanoid; stable_punch.pkl; 30-joint custom humanoid; vis_motion.py; MuJoCo XML/URDF; specific submission and version not mentioned.
translations.details.limits.0: This is a self-test by the author of the custom humanoid; the order of DOF indices by importers (sorted by name, tree structure, or XML order) needs verification in the target toolchain.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The questioner explicitly states the problem resolved and lists the two reasons and fixes mentioned.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: When redirecting a custom humanoid, the left key points align, but the right body is misaligned; how to diagnose the issue?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Incorrect axis signs or joint order can produce commands with opposite directions; verify with small single-joint commands before real machine testing.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Negative-axis joints in URDF are not compensated in dof_pos; NECK_Y is imported before the upper arm DOF, causing the right joint vector to misalign with the ROTATION_AXIS order.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Left arm and leg can match the red key points, but the right body cannot; changing a single axis sign does not resolve the issue.
translations.media_summaries.0: The original poster used red key points to describe left-right differences, but the root cause and fix are explicitly stated in the questioner's text; no additional conclusions from unreviewed screenshots were added.
translations.source.title: Custom Humanoid Re-direction Causes One Side Normal, the Other Key Points Misaligned: Negative Axis Sign and Joint Order Are Not Consistent
translations.title: How to Diagnose and Fix Axis Sign and Joint Order Mismatches in Custom Humanoid Re-directions Where One Side is Normal and the Other is Misaligned?
